text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Australian pioneer JOHN BINGLE, who ran the first trading ships between Sydney and Newcastle, was born in 1796.
American author LYMAN FRANK BAUM, who created the "Wizard Of Oz", was born in 1856.

French scientist PIERRE CURIE, who with his wife MARIE discovered radium in 1898, was born in 1859. Radium is a white, radioactive, metallic element, and one of its 16 isotopes (the commonest Ra-226) has a half-life of 1,622 years.
American author KATHERINE ANNE PORTER, who wrote mostly short stories (her only novel "Ship Of Fools" won a Pulitzer Prize in 1962), was born in 1890.

Australian author and adventurer ALFRED FRANCIS XAVIER HERBERT ("Poor Fellow My Country" published in 1975), who worked as a stockman, deep-sea diver and miner, was born in Port Hedland in Western Australia in 1901.
American actor JOSEPH COTTON, whose films included "Citizen Kane" and "The Third Man", was born in 1905.
British actor JAMES MASON, who was married to Australian actress CLARISSA KAYE and appeared in more than 80 films, was born in 1909.
Australian singer DARRYL STEWART was born in 1932.
Australian journalist and former current affairs host BILL PEACH was born in 1935.
British drummer with LULU, CAT STEVENS, JEFF BECK, Stealers Wheel and the Strawbs, ROD COOMBES, was born in 1946.
British composer and instrumentalist MIKE OLDFIELD, who had a big hit with "Tubular Bells", was born in 1953.
** EVENTS **
1718 : London lawyer JAMES PUCKLE patented a
multiple-barrelled revolving machine-gun.
1800 : JAMES HATFIELD attempted to assassinate KING
GEORGE III of England at the Drury Lane Theatre in London.
1829 : The American Congress designated the slave trade
as piracy.
1862 : The first sports ground designed purely for
baseball was opened in Brooklyn.
1918 : The world's first regular air-mail service between
Washington and New York was established.
1928 : The Royal Flying Doctor Service was launched in

Cloncurry in Queensland. Doctor K. ST VINCENT WELCH of the Australian Inland Mission Aerial Service launched the RFDS, with a DH50 aircraft and pilot provided by QANTAS (Queensland And Northern Territory Aerial Service).
1930 : The first-ever 'air hostess' (nurse ELLEN CHURCH)
took care of 11 passengers on a flight from Oakland (California) to Cheyenne (Wyoming).
1943 : A Japanese submarine torpedoed and sank the

Australian hospital ship "Centaur" off the east coast near Brisbane. 268 lives were lost in the biggest loss from a submarine attack in Australian waters. The American destroyer "Mugford" picked up 63 survivors, including the lone woman survivor, Sister ELLEN SAVAGE. The ship, which was brightly lit,

was struck about 4 am with a direct hit to a fuel tank. The ship caught fire and sank within three minutes. Most on board were asleep when the "Centaur" went down. In early April 1995 a Melbourne diver found the wreck of the ship near Moreton Island.
1957 : Britain's first hydrogen bomb was exploded at
Christmas Island in the central Pacific.
1972 : The Governor of Alabama GEORGE WALLACE was shot 5
times at close range by 21 year-old ARTHUR BREMER. He survived, and retired in 1987.
1987 : Australia's longest serving Prime Minister, Sir
ROBERT MENZIES, died.
1987 : American actress and dancer RITA HAYWORTH
(MARGARITA CARMEN CANSINO) died, after a long battle with Alzheimer's Disease.
1988 : The Soviet Union began withdrawing troops from
Afghanistan.
1989 : Half a million people gathered outside the "Great

Hall Of The People" in Peking (Beijing) demanding democratic reform, as Soviet President MICKAIL GORBACHEV and Chinese Premier DENG XIAOPING held talks aimed at healing the long-standing rift between the Communist nations.
1990 : Retired British brothel-keeper LINDA ST CLARE
(known professionally as "Miss Whiplash") lost a long-running court battle with the Inland Revenue over the payment of back taxes.
1991 : EDITH CRESSON replaced French Prime Minister
MICHEL ROCARD following his resignation.
